newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota unemployment falls to 3.3 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota unemployment falls to 3.3 pct in May.

text.p: Minnesota's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate fell from 3.4 percent in April to 3.3 percent in May, the Minnesota Department of Economic Security reported Thursday.
The state's unadjusted rate fell from 3.5 percent to 2.7 percent, the lowest level since the current method for calculating unemployment was adopted in 1978, the department said.

"We expected the unemployment rate to be higher this month because of the late spring and flooding," Commissioner R. Jane Brown said. "However, those two natural occurrences merely delayed regular hiring."
Minnesota's seasonally adjusted rate in May 1996 was 4 percent.
The national seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for May was 4.8 percent, down from 4.9 percent in April and 5.5 percent in May 1996.
